title: Barnes maze, a useful task to assess spatial reference memory in the mice
protocol: Place the mouse in a cylindrical black start chamber in the middle of the maze.
Lift the chamber after 10 seconds and switch on the buzzer.
Gently guide the mouse towards the escape box without forcing it into the hole.
If necessary, place the mouse gently to the side of the hole and pull the base of the tail to encourage entry into the escape box.
Turn off the buzzer, light, and/or fan once the mouse is inside the escape box.
Allow the mouse to stay in the escape box for 2 minutes.
Clean the maze with a solution containing 1% Incidin before each trial.
Rotate the maze around its central axis after each trial to control for possible odor cues.
Place the mouse in the cylindrical black start chamber in the middle of the maze.
Lift the chamber and turn on the buzzer after 10 seconds.
Allow the mouse to explore the maze for 3 minutes.
Measure the number of primary errors, total errors, and primary latency by the experimenter for 3 minutes.
End the trial when the mouse enters the goal tunnel or after 3 min have elapsed.
Turn off the buzzer immediately after the mouse enters the tunnel.
Allow the mouse to stay in the tunnel for 1 minute.
If the mouse does not reach the goal within 3 minutes, guide the mouse gently to the escape box.
Place the mouse inside the escape box for 1 minute.
Cover the escape hole once the mouse is inside for 1 minute or place mice gently back into the escape box whenever it goes out.
Return the mouse to its home cage until the next trial.
Repeat steps 4-9 until the animal has had the desired number of trials for that day, with 4 trials per day and an inter-trial interval (ITI) of 15 minutes over 4 days.
Use the ITI of 15 minutes to test the next 3 to 4 mice.
Conduct a probe trial on day 5, 24 hours after the last training day.
Close the target hole for the probe trial.
Rotate the maze so that the target hole is closed.
Re-adjust the maze to ensure the holes are in the same position as during the training days.
Place the animal in the middle of the maze under the cylindrical black start chamber.
Wait for 10 seconds, then lift the chamber and switch on the buzzer.
Allow the mouse to explore the maze for a fixed interval (90 s).
Remove the mouse after 90 seconds.
Measure the number of pokes (errors) in each hole during exploration.
Record the latency and path length to reach the target goal hole.
On day 12, conduct a second probe trial without any training sessions between days 5 and 12.
Repeat steps 12-15 for reference memory probe trials, ensuring they are performed at least 24 hours after the last training trial.
